about: Stage graph of the Scoring Sources lesson (Touch). Every number is copied from Addendum D (D3, D4b) or the Stage A progress log (registry EXP-037); nothing is computed here except the sums the check script asserts. No individual pair score and no trace is included: they stay sealed until the pilot closes.

stages.title: Inherited scores
stages.what: Scores made earlier for the pilot and for dev tuning, in three files. Same model (bge-reranker-v2-m3), int8 ONNX on Kaggle CPU.
stages.checks: That the three files agree where they overlap.

stages.title: New pairs to score
stages.what: Every (question, passage) pair of the widest graph walk, hops 0 to 2, for the 18 dev items and the 30 pilot items, plus the text arm's pairs.
stages.checks: That the collector wrote the count the protocol predicted.
stages.real: 195,471 unique keys collected: 13,841 already scored, 181,630 new. Dev 81,954 pairs, pilot 118,691.

stages.title: S1: same int8 job
stages.what: The job that made the inherited scores, with every setting pinned, split into 24 shards plus 1 timing probe.
stages.checks: Nothing yet. A kernel may score new pairs only after its overlap check passes.

stages.title: S2: one fp32 GPU job
stages.what: A full re-score of every key, the inherited ones included, with the full-precision checkpoint on one GPU. Specified before any pair was collected.
stages.checks: It runs only if the switch rule selects it.
stages.real: Not selected. The specification stays bound in stage 1.

stages.title: 200-key overlap check
stages.what: Before scoring anything new, each kernel re-scores the same 200 inherited keys, drawn with a fixed seed from 10,622 keys with known pair text.
stages.checks: Every one of the 200 scores must be bit-equal to the stored score. int8 results can depend on the CPU instruction set, so each kernel also logs its CPU flags.
stages.real: Every kernel matched 200/200, on both CPU types: Intel Xeon 2.20 GHz and AMD EPYC 7B12. 0 mismatches.

stages.title: Mac diagnostic
stages.what: A side test on a Mac (ARM CPU), outside the switch rule: 50 pairs of the overlap sample.
stages.checks: Whether a different CPU type gives the same int8 numbers.
stages.real: Same order (Spearman 0.987), different numbers: bit-equal 0/50, max |Δ| 0.104. This is why the check exists.

stages.title: Switch rule
stages.what: S1 stays only if every kernel was bit-equal on all 200 keys. One mismatch anywhere selects S2 for every key.
stages.checks: Equality only. Speed, cost and wall-clock time are not criteria.
stages.real: S1. The switch record was committed before the merge.

stages.title: Merge
stages.what: One file: the inherited scores plus the new S1 scores. A key already scored keeps its inherited score.
stages.checks: No key has two different scores.

stages.title: Coverage
stages.what: Every pair the collector produced must have a score.
stages.checks: The merge refuses anything below 100 % coverage.

stages.title: Stage 2: bound before tuning
stages.what: The pair list and the merged score file are hashed and committed. Dev tuning then reads only this file.
stages.checks: dev_tune refuses a score file whose hash differs from stage 2.
stages.real: Dev re-tuning ran on it: s7-b/2 with k_graph 30. I4 (7cae3a31) binds it. Per-item rows are sealed until the pilot closes.

demo.label: rule demo, not a run
demo.what: What the frozen rule does if one kernel finds one key that differs.
demo.outcome: S2: every key re-scored by the GPU job; the S1 scores from passing kernels are discarded.
